text:
maya singh: quick check-in — ran the overnight sweep (AWQ + int8 fallback) on the new gpt-7b-green snapshot with prefix-KV cache + continuous-batcher. results are... odd :thinking:
jeremy cho: odd how? numbers plz
sophia li: can you include the eval set and the config used? might be dataset shift
maya singh: short summary: AWQ quant -> ~2.8% EM drop on NQ eval vs fp16 baseline, int8 fallback reduces drop to ~1.1% but increases p95 latency by ~12%. overall throughput up ~16% at our 64-concurrency steady-state. prefix cache hitrate dropped from 82% -> 65% when AWQ active.
jeremy cho: prefix cache drop is concerning. any pattern by prompt length? :eyes:
maya singh: yes — longer prefixes (>=256 tokens) see bigger hitrate loss. hypothesis: quantized KV fingerprint collisions or canonicalization mismatch in serialization path.
perf-bot: perf-bot report ready — 2158642000: AWQ-sweep v3, samples=10k, p50=93ms, p95=210ms, throughput=4.6k req/min, kv-hit=65%
ops-claire: did you reproduce on dedicated nodes or hosted? could be driver differences
maya singh: dedicated infra w/ driver v2.3 + runtime patch r128. reproduced on a small on-prem rig (same kernel).
sophia li: paste the batching config? curious if continuous-batcher coalescing strategy changed token interleaving
maya singh: config snippet:
```
batcher:
  type: continuous
  max_batch_size: 64
  max_latency_ms: 12
  coalesce_window_ms: 6
kv_cache:
  mode: prefix
  ttl_ms: 300000
  serialization: snakebuf-v2
quant:
  backend: awq
  fallback: int8
  calibration_samples: 512
```
jeremy cho: snakebuf-v2 serialization was introduced in r126. maybe AWQ's packing expects snakebuf-v1 layout -> misaligned keys. can you run a small repro that toggles serialization?
maya singh: running now: toggled to snakebuf-v1 -> kv-hit jumps to 80%, EM drop reduces to 0.9% (AWQ-only). latency regresses a bit vs v2 but overall SLA still ok. looks like packing mismatch.
sophia li: so two effects: (1) serialization mismatch reduces cache effectiveness, (2) continuous-batcher pulls in different token alignments when quantized kernels change token-level timing -> causes slightly different micro-batching boundaries and warmup behavior. both together amplify quality delta.
jeremy cho: good find. next steps: 1) add a check in model onboarding to assert serialization compatibility for quant backends, 2) add a canary that measures kv-hit delta when turning on quant backend, 3) instrument per-prefix checksum in cache to detect packing mismatches early.
maya singh: agreed. I'll open a PR with a unit test that runs small serialization roundtrip and a perf smoke test that compares kv-hit >= baseline-5%.
perf-bot: perf-bot note: create ticket ML-SEQ-4578 for serialization-compat check (linked to pr#4321)
ops-claire: FYI running a cluster-wide rollout will need a graceful fallback policy: if kv-hit drops >10% in canary, auto-fallback to fp16 or int8 variant.
sophia li: also let's include eval slices by prefix-length in the daily regression dashboard. this would have flagged the 256+ token effect earlier.
maya singh: will add slices and schedule another overnight with snakebuf-v1 vs v2 to quantify latency/quality tradeoff.
jeremy cho: thanks — great triage. small win: not an algorithmic AWQ failure, more infra/compat fragility. :thumbsup:
maya singh: cc @eng-runtime for kernel timing diffs — may affect coalescing heuristics.
